purpose: Firstcall PR4a, approved by Cristian 2026-11-21 (plan rev 2): a salesperson can record or upload a short voice memo on a lead page; it becomes a Voice note transcribed locally by Whisper, with no model key and no spend, and the contact they picked is logged at once. It also freezes the seed-11 voice gold and its scorer before any transcription code, for PR4b's eval.
mechanism: Upload: POST of raw audio to the lead's voice route. The route checks who may record, then the per-person (3 waiting memos) and per-org (600 s waiting) caps without a lock, takes one of 2 per-process check slots, reads the body to at most 5 MB, sniffs the format from the first bytes (webm, mp4/m4a, wav, mp3, ogg) and requires the declared type to fit, then writes it to an unnamed temp file that ffprobe and ffmpeg read as /dev/fd/N with a forced demuxer and only the file protocol, measuring length by decoding (over 180 s is 422). Under the org lock it rechecks the caps and in one transaction saves the note (source voice, read state transcribing), the voice_audio row and a transcribe job, and logs the picked contact. Transcriber: a separate process (firstcall worker --kind transcribe; compose service transcriber under the voice profile, 2 CPUs, 1536m, whisper-models volume, built from the Dockerfile's voice stage which adds the voice dependency group). In local mode it checks ffmpeg and ffprobe, imports faster-whisper and loads the pinned model before claiming any job, and exits 1 naming the cause if any fails. It claims only transcribe jobs; the main worker never does. A transcription runs in three steps with an attempt check; lease renewal survives database errors and writes the heartbeat. Success fills the note text, sets it pending, queues read_note and deletes the audio in one transaction. Unusable audio fails at once; other errors retry until attempts run out; the scheduler's expire step fails any memo still waiting after 30 minutes; every failure path sets failed/not_transcribed and deletes the audio. Database errors are logged and stored as class plus SQLSTATE only, and the engine hides bound parameters. Page: under the note form, Record a memo / Stop and send with a timer (auto-stop at 2:59.5) and Send a recording; the form is busy from Record or a picked file until the upload answers; a Voice badge, Transcribing..., the transcript, or Couldn't transcribe this memo. Dependencies: the voice group is not in uv's default groups; typings/faster_whisper/__init__.pyi lets pyright check the two calls; numpy is in dev for the transcriber tests; ffmpeg is in the app image and CI. Gold: evals/gold/voice holds 300 clips (150 seed-11 scripts, clean and degraded, 10 voices), spoken.jsonl, clips.jsonl, the name-spellings table and a manifest; firstcall/evaluation/voice_score.py adds WER and scores names by sound for voice only, with the strict spelling count on its own line.
decisions: Separate transcriber process so a memo never holds up new-lead alerts. Audio waits in Postgres at most 30 minutes. Voice names scored by sound (Cristian's choice), strict count still shown. The voice group left out of default installs because onnxruntime and av have no wheels for Intel macOS or macOS 13; a type stub keeps pyright resolving faster-whisper, and the real run in the voice image guards against stub drift. Uploads go through an unnamed temp file, not a pipe, because an MP4 indexed last cannot be decoded from a pipe, and so a crash leaves no recording on disk. PR4a must be merged with a merge commit so the gold-before-code history test holds on main.
readers: README.md: people running Firstcall locally. docs/board.md and docs/adr/ADR-005-local-transcription.md: maintainers and reviewers of the board and the transcription choice. Comments in firstcall/voice, firstcall/board, firstcall/pipeline, migrations, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, verify.sh, web/src: the next maintainer.
